issues.description: This image has no description for people who cannot see it.
issues.suggestion: Add a short, meaningful description of what the image shows, or mark it as decorative if it is purely decorative.
issues.description_technical: The element is missing the alt attribute entirely, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A blind user relying on a screen reader hears nothing when this image is reached and loses the information it conveys.
issues.why_technical: Screen readers expose the alt attribute as the accessible name of the img element; without it, the AT announces the filename or 'image', providing no semantic value.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add alt="" to the element, or alt="" if the image is purely decorative.

issues.description: The image has an alt attribute that contains a filename ("icecream.jpg") instead of a meaningful description of the image content.
issues.suggestion: Replace the alt text with a concise description of what the image shows, e.g., "Space station orbiting Mars".
issues.description_technical: The alt attribute value "icecream.jpg " is not a meaningful text alternative; it is a filename with a trailing space, which fails to convey the purpose or content of the image, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions) as it does not provide an appropriate label for the image.
issues.why_simple: A blind user relying on a screen reader will hear "icecream.jpg" which gives no useful information about the image, making the content inaccessible.
issues.why_technical: Screen readers announce the alt attribute value; a filename like "icecream.jpg" is not descriptive and does not fulfill the requirement for a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose of the image.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change the alt attribute to a meaningful description: alt="Space station orbiting Mars".

issues.description: This image has no alt attribute at all, so it is completely unlabeled for assistive technology users.
issues.suggestion: Add an alt attribute with a brief description of the image, or alt="" if it is purely decorative.
issues.description_technical: The img element lacks an alt attribute, which is required for all images to provide a text alternative. Without it, screen readers may announce the filename or nothing, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions).
issues.why_simple: A blind user will not know what this image is about; they may hear the filename or nothing, making the image invisible to them.
issues.why_technical: The absence of an alt attribute means assistive technologies have no text alternative to present, failing the requirement that all non-text content have a text alternative.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add alt="Mars spaceman illustration" or alt="" if decorative.

issues.description: The alt text "thumbnail-image" is generic and does not describe the specific content or function of the image.

issues.description_technical: The alt attribute value "thumbnail-image" is not descriptive; it does not convey the purpose or content of the image, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions) as it fails to provide a meaningful label.
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user hears "thumbnail-image" which gives no information about what the image actually shows, making it useless.
issues.why_technical: Assistive technologies rely on alt text to convey the equivalent information; a generic label like "thumbnail-image" does not fulfill the requirement for a text alternative that serves the same purpose as the image.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change the alt attribute to a meaningful description: alt="Channel logo for Mars Exploration".

issues.description: The alt text 'icecream.jpg' is a filename, not a meaningful description, and does not match the image content (space station).

issues.why_technical: Assistive technology uses the alt attribute as the accessible name. A filename does not provide meaningful information, failing WCAG 4.1.2.

issues.description: The alt text has a trailing space, which may cause inconsistent announcement by screen readers.
issues.suggestion: Remove the trailing space from the alt text.

issues.why_technical: Trailing whitespace in alt attributes can cause assistive technology to misinterpret the accessible name, failing WCAG 4.1.2.

issues.why_simple: A blind user will hear a description that does not match the actual image, causing confusion.
issues.why_technical: The accessible name must accurately convey the image's purpose or content. A mismatch fails WCAG 4.1.2.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change alt="Martian sunrise." to alt="Global free days" or appropriate description based on actual image content.

issues.description: An SVG image has no accessible name, so screen readers cannot describe it.

issues.description_technical: The <svg> element lacks role="img" and an accessible name via aria-label, aria-labelledby, or a <title> element. According to WCAG 1.1.1, all non-text content must have a text alternative. Informative SVGs need an accessible name; decorative SVGs should have aria-hidden="true".
issues.why_simple: A blind user will not know what the SVG represents, missing important visual information.
issues.why_technical: Screen readers may ignore the SVG or announce it as an unnamed graphic, failing to convey its purpose.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add role="img" and aria-label="Description of the SVG" or include a <title> element inside the SVG. If decorative, add aria-hidden="true" and focusable="false".

issues.description: The page title describes a technical helper function rather than the actual content of the page, which appears to be about Mars exploration images.
issues.suggestion: Change the page title to accurately describe the content, e.g., 'Mars Exploration Image Gallery'.
issues.description_technical: The <title> element content 'Facebook Cross-Domain Messaging helper' does not describe the page's visible content (Mars images), violating WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.2 (Page Titled).
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user cannot tell what this page is about from the title, making it hard to navigate or find the page again.
issues.why_technical: The title is the first thing announced by screen readers and appears in browser tabs; a misleading title disorients users and fails to provide a meaningful page identifier.
issues.suggestion_technical: Replace <title>Facebook Cross-Domain Messaging helper</title> with <title>Mars Exploration Image Gallery</title>.

issues.description: The page has no <main> landmark, making it difficult for screen reader users to navigate directly to the primary content.
issues.suggestion: Wrap the primary content in a <main> element.
issues.description_technical: The page lacks a <main> element or role="main", violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and SC 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks).
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user cannot skip to the main content and must navigate through all elements sequentially.
issues.why_technical: Landmarks provide navigation shortcuts; without a main landmark, users cannot quickly jump to the primary content region.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add <main> around the main content of the page, e.g., <main>...images...</main>.
